links.outcome: Glaucoma detection AUC across race and age subgroups
links.effect: Performance consistent across race and age: Black (AUC = 0.87) vs. other (AUC = 0.86), and >60 years (AUC = 0.84) vs. <60 years (AUC = 0.87).
links.quote: Performance was consistent across race and age for all training size and cycle number combinations: Black (AUC = 0.87) vs. other (AUC = 0.86), and >60 years (AUC = 0.84) vs. <60 years (AUC = 0.87).

links.outcome: AUC by fine-tuning sample size and training epochs
links.effect: AUC rose from 0.52 (50 images, 5 epochs) to 0.86 (2000 images, 50 epochs); 0.82 at ~500 and 0.83 at ~1000 images, with diminishing gains.
links.quote: Performance increased with larger training datasets and more training cycles, improving from 50 training images and 5 epochs (AUC: 0.52) to 2000 training images and 50 epochs (AUC: 0.86), with reduced gain in performance from approximately 500 and 1000 training images (AUC of 0.82 and 0.83, respectively).

screen.reason: The study evaluates an existing ophthalmic foundation model (RETFound) for glaucoma detection across varied training sample sizes and demographic subgroups (racial and age equity). It benchmarks diagnostic performance without testing specific organizational deployment practices or safeguards.
